concerns.text: The specification relies exclusively on twelve simple compositional descriptors (atomic radius, electronegativity, oxidation state, valence electron count for A, B, X sites) and does not provide any contingency plan or justification for why these descriptors alone should capture defect formation energies, which are known to depend on local structural and electronic environments. Constitution VI requires an escalation justification if baseline compositional models fail to meet the RMSE <0.5 eV target, but the spec contains no such fallback (e.g., inclusion of structural descriptors, crystal graph features, or more advanced models). This methodological gap risks model misspecification and undermines the validity of the claimed success criteria.
